title: metadata-protocol + types: a batch row error whose throw declares a non-finite status ships `httpStatus: null`
body:
domain:server#7 · os-sales · session_01L6bhgVSjQBHNkZd6Eqx2XX

Follow-up of #32250 (PR #32740), from the card thread's report on head `08fa3a2f0`; filed on the epic seat's direction. Not a merge blocker. Parked under ruling 6824949405 on #31527.

## What happens

`resolveThrownHttpError` (`packages/types/src/thrown-http-error.ts`) takes `declaredStatus` from `typeof e.status === 'number'` (else `statusCode`). `NaN` and `Infinity` are numbers, so a throw that declares one yields `declaredStatus: NaN`. `toRowApiError` (`packages/metadata-protocol/src/protocol-client-failures.ts`) then stamps `httpStatus: declaredStatus` on the batch row's error, and JSON serialises it as `httpStatus: null`.

This is the behaviour on `main` as well (read at `f7a0fe0ea`: the `typeof … === 'number'` limb predates PR #32740). No in-tree producer throws a non-finite status; every declared status in the tree is a literal.

## What is owed

1. Measure on `main`: a hook throwing `{ status: NaN }` (and `Infinity`, `statusCode: NaN`) on a per-row door (`updateMany`, `/:object/batch`) and on a whole-request door; record the row's `httpStatus`, `code` and the whole-request status.
2. Decide the TO in this card: treat a non-finite (or non-integer, or out-of-range) declaration as undeclared — the row carries no `httpStatus` and the whole-request door answers by the undeclared rule — or keep the value under a stated rule. Read the declaration in one place so the resolver, `mapDataError`'s `declaredHttpStatus` and `toRowApiError` agree.
3. Pin each door (red before, green after).

## Acceptance

No row error ships `httpStatus: null`; the three readers agree on what counts as a declared status; declared finite statuses answer exactly as before.

Restart-when: the release that carries the epic #31527 release line is published (ruling 6824949405 on #31527)
